sentences.text: When Zarathustra was thirty years old, he left his home and the lake of his home, and went into the mountains.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: Zarathustra’s Prologue

sentences.text: There he enjoyed his spirit and solitude, and for ten years did not weary of it.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: Zarathustra’s Prologue

sentences.text: Where solitude endeth, there beginneth the market-place; and where the market-place beginneth, there beginneth also the noise of the great actors, and the buzzing of the poison-flies.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Flies in the Market-Place

sentences.text: Flee, my friend, into thy solitude!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Flies in the Market-Place

sentences.text: I see thee deafened with the noise of the great men, and stung all over with the stings of the little ones.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Flies in the Market-Place

sentences.text: Flee thither, where a rough, strong breeze bloweth!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Flies in the Market-Place

sentences.text: Life is a well of delight; but where the rabble also drink, there all fountains are poisoned.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Rabble

sentences.text: Choose the GOOD solitude, the free, wanton, lightsome solitude, which also gives you the right still to remain good in any sense whatsoever!
sentences.work: Beyond Good and Evil: The Free Spirit

sentences.text: For solitude is a virtue with us, as a sublime bent and bias to purity, which divines that in the contact of man and man--"in society"--it must be unavoidably impure.
sentences.work: Beyond Good and Evil: What Is Noble?

sentences.text: All society makes one somehow, somewhere, or sometime--"commonplace."
sentences.work: Beyond Good and Evil: What Is Noble?

sentences.text: Verily, to the loftiest height had I to fly, to find again the well of delight!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Rabble

sentences.text: Oh, I have found it, my brethren!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Rabble

sentences.text: Here on the loftiest height bubbleth up for me the well of delight!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Rabble

sentences.text: And there is a life at whose waters none of the rabble drink with me!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Rabble

sentences.text: For this is OUR height and our home: too high and steep do we here dwell for all uncleanly ones and their thirst.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Rabble

sentences.text: When aloft, I find myself always alone.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Tree on the Hill

sentences.text: No one speaketh unto me; the frost of solitude maketh me tremble.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Tree on the Hill

sentences.text: What do I seek on the height?
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Tree on the Hill

sentences.text: The more he seeketh to rise into the height and light, the more vigorously do his roots struggle earthward, downward, into the dark and deep—into the evil.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Tree on the Hill

sentences.text: On the open height wouldst thou be; for the stars thirsteth thy soul.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Tree on the Hill

sentences.text: But thy bad impulses also thirst for freedom.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Tree on the Hill

sentences.text: In solitude there groweth what any one bringeth into it—also the brute in one’s nature.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Higher Man

sentences.text: Thus is solitude inadvisable unto many.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Higher Man

sentences.text: The highest instinct for purity places him who is affected with it in the most extraordinary and dangerous isolation, as a saint: for it is just holiness--the highest spiritualization of the instinct in question.
sentences.work: Beyond Good and Evil: What Is Noble?

sentences.text: In the writings of a recluse one always hears something of the echo of the wilderness, something of the murmuring tones and timid vigilance of solitude; in his strongest words, even in his cry itself, there sounds a new and more dangerous kind of silence, of concealment.
sentences.work: Beyond Good and Evil: What Is Noble?

sentences.text: But one day will the solitude weary thee; one day will thy pride yield, and thy courage quail.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Way of the Creating One

sentences.text: Thou wilt one day cry: “I am alone!”
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Way of the Creating One

sentences.text: Thus passed with the lonesome one months and years; his wisdom meanwhile increased, and caused him pain by its abundance.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Child with the Mirror

sentences.text: His soul, however, became impatient and full of longing for those whom he loved: because he had still much to give them.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Child with the Mirror

sentences.text: For this is hardest of all: to close the open hand out of love, and keep modest as a giver.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Child with the Mirror

sentences.text: Thou great star!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: Zarathustra’s Prologue

sentences.text: What would be thy happiness if thou hadst not those for whom thou shinest!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: Zarathustra’s Prologue

sentences.text: Passion for power: but who would call it PASSION, when the height longeth to stoop for power!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Three Evil Things

sentences.text: Verily, nothing sick or diseased is there in such longing and descending!
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Three Evil Things

sentences.text: Now do the waves rise and rise around thy mountain, O Zarathustra.

sentences.text: And however high be thy height, many of them must rise up to thee: thy boat shall not rest much longer on dry ground.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Greeting

sentences.text: Too long have I longed and looked into the distance.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Child with the Mirror

sentences.text: Too long hath solitude possessed me: thus have I unlearned to keep silence.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Child with the Mirror

sentences.text: By divers ways and wendings did I arrive at my truth; not by one ladder did I mount to the height where mine eye roveth into my remoteness.
sentences.work: Thus Spake Zarathustra: The Spirit of Gravity

sentences.text: Out of the deepest must the highest come to its height.—
